title: How Much Does HVAC SEO Cost? 2026 Pricing for HVAC Companies
html:
HVAC SEO cost runs $1,000 to $5,000 a month for most HVAC companies. One-time projects like a site audit cost $2,000 to $10,000, and hourly help runs $100 to $300. Where you land depends on keyword competition, your website's condition, and how many services and cities you want to rank for. A site with crawl or speed problems often needs HVAC technical SEO services first. This guide breaks down each pricing model, what pushes cost up, and how to build a budget around the leads you need.

5 Factors That Drive HVAC SEO Cost

Factor What it adds Example
Keyword competition $1,500 to $3,000/mo for competitive terms, $500 to $1,500/mo for easier ones "AC repair" in a big metro costs more than "duct cleaning"
Website condition $1,000 to $5,000 upfront for a dated site, $500 to $1,500 for a modern one A slow site with broken links costs more to fix
Service scope $2,000 to $5,000/mo for full SEO, $500 to $1,500/mo for local SEO only AC, furnace, and ductless pages cost more than one "HVAC repair" page
Business size $3,000 to $10,000/mo for regional or multi-service companies, $1,000 to $3,000/mo for local shops A regional chain targets broader terms than a single-location shop
Seasonality $500 to $1,000/mo extra ahead of summer and winter peaks Publishing "AC installation" content in March so it ranks by June

How to Estimate Your HVAC SEO Budget in 6 Steps

Build your budget backward from the leads you need, and use HVAC call tracking to see which leads turn into booked jobs and revenue. 1. Set a lead goal. Say you want 20 leads a month. At a 10% conversion rate, you need 200 organic visitors a month. 2. Pick target keywords. Use Google Keyword Planner to find buying-intent terms like "emergency AC repair" and "furnace installation," and note how competitive each one is. 3. Check your website. Run Google PageSpeed Insights and a Screaming Frog crawl. A site that loads in 5 seconds may need about $2,000 of work to reach 2 seconds. 4. Choose a pricing model. A $1,500 to $3,000 retainer fits ongoing growth. A $2,000 to $5,000 project fits a one-time fix. 5. Add it up, plus a buffer. "AC repair" ($1,500) plus "HVAC maintenance" ($800) comes to $2,300. Add 20% for seasonal pushes, and you get $2,760 a month. 6. Start small and scale. Begin around $1,000 a month and track leads in Google Analytics. If "furnace installation" brings 15 leads at $1,500 a month, raise the budget there first.

5 Ways to Get More From Your HVAC SEO Budget

  • Start with local SEO. Verify your Google Business Profile, keep your name, address, and phone number identical across directories, and target "near me" terms. Local SEO alone runs $500 to $1,500 a month.
  • Build a page for each service and city. Separate pages for AC repair, furnace installation, and duct cleaning rank better than one services list.
  • Publish content homeowners search for. Posts of 800 to 1,500 words, like "How to Maintain Your HVAC System," cost $200 to $500 each and keep bringing traffic after you publish.
  • Speed up your site with technical SEO services. Compress images and turn on caching. Expect $500 to $2,000 upfront, and aim for under 3 seconds on mobile.
  • Track and adjust monthly. Use Google Analytics and Search Console to see which pages bring leads, then put more budget behind those pages.

What Should You Budget for HVAC SEO?

Most HVAC companies should budget $1,000 to $5,000 a month for SEO. Local shops targeting a few services land near the low end. Regional companies chasing competitive terms like "AC repair" land near the top.

What’s the average HVAC SEO cost for HVAC companies?

The average SEO budget for a typical local business in the HVAC industry ranges from $1,000 to $5,000 per month. This SEO cost heavily depends on the competitiveness of your target keywords, the need for technical SEO on your HVAC company website, and the overall scope of your HVAC SEO services.

Is SEO worth it for HVAC companies?

Yes, if you give it 3 to 6 months. Organic leads keep coming without a per-click cost, so your cost per lead drops as rankings grow. For example, a $2,000 monthly retainer that brings in 20 leads works out to $100 per lead, and that figure falls as more pages rank.
